transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-17
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Luis Martinez (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (Cumulus ML Lead), Tom Reynolds (Infra), Priya Kapoor (Security), Jared Lee (Data Scientist)

[00:00] Ava: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, can you all hear me?
[00:03] Maya: Yeah, loud and clear.
[00:06] Luis: good afternoon from our side. quick agenda: review the INT8/FP8 runs we ran this week, dig into perf deltas and any quality regressions, then decide next experiments.
[00:18] Maya: Sounds good. Just to orient folks, we ran the internal clinical QA set (1k prompts), and a smaller labelled subset for human eval (200). we used the same temperature/decoding as baseline.
[00:28] Samir: right, we kept sampling seeds consistent. high-level summary: FP8 - about 1.2x token throughput vs FP16 baseline on your staging GPU (A100X approximated), quality delta ~ -0.2% on our automatic QA metric, and human-eval indistinguishable in the 200 sample subset. INT8 - ~1.8x throughput, and we saw ~0.9% drop on the auto QA metric and a small uptick in hallucinations in edge prompts.
[00:48] Tom: when you say A100X approximated, we're running on our dedicated G5 fleet; the perf numbers were extrapolated by Redwood, right?
[00:56] Luis: yeah we profiled on cluster with similar memory characteristics; for the G5 we expect slightly better FP8 perf but INT8 kernel maturity on that card is still... like, variable, so we recommended running the end-to-end sweep.
[01:12] Maya: can you show the sheet? I think you uploaded the results?
[01:16] Ava: yes link in chat - Benchmark spreadsheet (short link: https://redwood.internal/benchmarks/CH-quant-2026-11).
[01:25] [screen share noise]
[01:30] Samir: scrolling - here's the baseline FP16, then FP8 (we used bfloat-style simulated FP8 path), INT8 uses GPTQ-derived weights + per-channel scale. Note the p50/p95/p99 columns: INT8 reduces p50 by 30%, p95 by ~25%, but p99 improvement is smaller and has a few outliers.
[01:54] Priya: are those outliers correlated with specific prompt lengths or KV cache warmup?
[02:00] Samir: good question, we looked at sequence length: spikes at >1024 tokens. also cold-start behavior when KV cache misses and when batching changes.
[02:10] Jared: on the quality side, the QA accuracy drop - is that spread across intents or concentrated? We care most about critical extraction fields.
[02:18] Luis: largely concentrated in long-form summary prompts and cases where the model needs to preserve exact numeric tokens (lab values). short intent classification is mostly intact.
[02:26] Maya: ok that maps to what we saw - extraction of lab codes had more errors. are these tokenization or quantization artifacts?
[02:32] Samir: mix of both; quantization can amplify small weights leading to occasional token choice changes. we also saw one-off tokenization mismaps in clinical codes - likely the tokenizer + subword boundary sensitivity.
[02:42] Tom: any mitigations? we discussed per-layer mixed precision before.
[02:46] Samir: yes. options: 1) per-layer mixed quant (keep first N layers in FP16, quantize the rest), 2) calibration with a representative dataset emphasizing numeric tokens, 3) bias-correction post-quant, 4) group-wise quantization or per-channel scales. For INT8 we recommend mixed-per-layer + calibration first. For FP8, a simple calibration set already got us almost baseline accuracy.
[03:10] Maya: what's the effort to run mixed-per-layer? time-wise?
[03:14] Samir: scripts run in about 2-3 hours for the model at your weight size on a single GPU for calibration, plus export time. The longer task is the human eval and verifying the extraction fields; that needs labeling.
[03:28] Maya: we can do the 500 labeled QA holdout but need timeframe - team bandwidth next week OK.
[03:34] Ava: we'll note that as action - Maya, 500 labeled examples by end of week?
[03:38] Maya: we'll aim for 2026-11-22.
[03:41] [small cross talk]
[03:44] Priya: security question - INT8/FP8 models, do they change our compliance surface? like, do quantized weights still get stored in KMS-encrypted buckets?
[03:53] Luis: no change in encryption or KMS handling. we still ship the artifact as an encrypted blob and you can store it in your S3/VPC bucket; Redwood's Private deploy keeps the control plane interactions under your VPC. the only difference is model size is smaller for INT8, but encryption and audit logs remain the same.
[04:10] Priya: ok, can you add the exact S3 lifecycle + KMS note to the security doc you shared?
[04:14] Ava: yeah we'll append a short section. link we shared earlier: Security pack (https://redwood.internal/security/CH-pack).
[04:21] Maya: back to perf - what about latency tail when batching changes quickly? Our traffic is bursty during end-of-day ingest windows.
[04:29] Luis: we saw INT8 can increase throughput but the batching heuristics need tuning. for bursty traffic FP8 might be safer to get consistent tails because the kernels are slightly more consistent. with INT8 you need smarter batching and more aggressive pre-warming of KV cache.
[04:43] Tom: can Redwood provide autoscaling policy templates for this workload?
[04:47] Ava: yes, under Redwood Dedicated we have policy templates: burst window sizing, pre-warm hints, and a recommended fallback to FP16 if p99 exceeds threshold. we'll share that.
[04:57] Samir: also consider prefix caching for common prompts - that reduces token compute and helps tails.
[05:03] Maya: any notable failure modes you saw in the 200 human eval?
[05:07] Jared: I can speak to that - in the 200 sample human eval INT8 had 5 cases of hallucinated lab names, FP8 had 1 ambiguous case. The human evaluators flagged where the answer deviated from extracts.
[05:19] Luis: those 5 cases are the ones we want to run through per-layer mixed quant and see if keeping some layers at FP16 fixes them.
[05:27] Samir: we also found that applying a small softmax temperature tweak after quantization sometimes mitigates token bias for numeric tokens. it's brittle but worth testing.
[05:36] Maya: interesting. how do we prioritize tests? I'd like to see: a) INT8 mixed-per-layer + calibration run, b) FP8 full sweep on our actual G5 fleet, c) 500-sample human-eval.
[05:47] Ava: good list. We'll own a and b with your infra help; you'll own c (Maya/Jared).
[05:53] Tom: I'll run the INT8 perf sweep in staging and upload the p50/p95/p99 and error traces to the sheet. Expect around 36 hours for a thorough run.
[06:02] Ava: note in actions.
[06:05] [pause, small typing sounds]
[06:10] Priya: second security item - audit logs for model downloads and inference: do quantized model downloads generate separate audit events?
[06:17] Luis: yes we log model build/export events and model pull events; your audit retention policy still applies. We'll add sample log entries to the pack.
[06:25] Maya: what's the recommended acceptance criteria for us to move forward with INT8 in production?
[06:30] Samir: we'd propose: auto-QA delta <= 0.5% from FP16 baseline on the heldout 500 sample, human-eval delta <= 1% top-line accuracy, and p99 latency no worse than 1.1x baseline during your peak window. If those hold, INT8 is viable.
[06:47] Maya: that seems fair.
[06:50] Ava: quick pricing note - INT8 can reduce GPU hours per token so estimated cost savings ~20-30% on throughput-normalized basis. I'll send updated pricing for reserve sizing.
[07:02] Tom: do you have an estimate for Dedicated commit we discussed last week?
[07:06] Ava: I'll attach an updated sheet after this call (Ava to send pricing).
[07:10] [longer pause - people looking at sheet]
[07:20] Luis: technical nit - when doing per-layer mixed quant, start by keeping the first 3 transformer blocks in FP16; that tends to preserve early tokenization-sensitive behavior. we also saw that quantizing the final LM head is often risky; keep LM head in FP16 if possible.
[07:34] Samir: on tooling: we'll push the GPTQ scripts we used plus a small wrapper that does per-layer exports and a small calibration script to collect scales using your representative dataset.
[07:45] Maya: that will help. also please document the exact tokenizer version used; we had one mismatch earlier between our tokenization and export pipeline which caused some numeric token shifts.
[07:56] Luis: good call - tokenizer version and merges file will be included.
[08:01] Ava: ok, recap and next steps: Samir to send scripts and README (due 11/19), Tom to run INT8 perf sweep and upload results (due 11/20), Maya/Jared to provide 500 labeled holdout (due 11/22), Ava to share updated pricing and append security note to pack (due 11/18). We'll tentatively meet next week 11/24 to review results.
[08:22] Maya: thanks, that works.
[08:25] Priya: thanks everyone.
[08:28] Ava: thanks all, we'll follow up in email with links. Bye.

End of transcript.
